content.thinking: The bash substitution `${f/.in./.out}` replaces ".in." with ".out" (not ".out."). Let me fix with sed/python. I'll write a Python test driver instead.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && cat > tmp/ncheck.py <<'EOF'
import subprocess, sys, pathlib
ok=True
for f in sorted(pathlib.Path('/workspace/examples').glob('*.in.native')):
    exp = f.with_name(f.name.replace('.in.','.out.'))
    data = f.read_bytes()
    r = subprocess.run([sys.argv[1]], input=data, capture_output=True)
    got = r.stdout.decode().split()
    want = exp.read_bytes().decode().split()
    if r.returncode or got != want:
        ok=False
        print('DIFF', f.name, r.returncode, r.stderr.decode()[:200])
        print(' got:', ' '.join(got)[:400])
        print(' exp:', ' '.join(want)[:400])
    else:
        print('MATCH', f.name)
print('NATIVE_OK' if ok else 'NATIVE_FAIL')
EOF
python3 tmp/ncheck.py /workspace/tmp/engine2
